executiveSummary.description: Upgraded Spring Boot parent from 2.7.18 to 3.5.16 to enable Java 25 compatibility, updated java.version from 1.8 to 25, migrated javax.servlet to jakarta.servlet, and added explicit UTF-8 charsets to FileWriter and getBytes() calls. The project compiles successfully with mvn clean compile and mvn verify on Java 25.

fixedUpdates.title: Upgrade Spring Boot parent from 2.7.18 to 3.5.16 for Java 25 compatibility
fixedUpdates.impact: Spring Boot 2.7.18 uses Spring Framework 5.3 whose ASM class reader cannot parse Java 25 class files, causing 'Unsupported class file major version' errors at start-up. Spring Boot 3.5.16 is the compatible release for Java 25.

fixedUpdates.title: Update java.version from 1.8 to 25 for Java 25 compilation
fixedUpdates.impact: Spring Boot 3.5+ requires Java 17+ as a minimum. Setting java.version to 25 ensures the compiler targets Java 25 class files as required by the upgrade target.

fixedUpdates.title: Migrate javax.servlet.http.HttpSession import to jakarta.servlet.http.HttpSession
fixedUpdates.impact: Spring Boot 3 brings Jakarta EE 9 where javax.* enterprise packages become jakarta.*. The javax.servlet import would not resolve, causing a compile error.

fixedUpdates.title: Add explicit UTF-8 charset to FileWriter to preserve encoding behavior on Java 18+
fixedUpdates.impact: Since Java 18 (JEP 400), the default charset is UTF-8. Adding an explicit StandardCharsets.UTF_8 preserves the intended UTF-8 encoding behavior and makes it explicit rather than relying on the platform default change.

fixedUpdates.title: Add explicit UTF-8 charset to String.getBytes() in MD5 hash computation
fixedUpdates.impact: Since Java 18 (JEP 400), String.getBytes() without a charset uses UTF-8 instead of the platform default. Adding an explicit StandardCharsets.UTF_8 makes the encoding deterministic and preserves the intended UTF-8 behavior.

fixedUpdates.title: Add java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets import to ReportService.java
fixedUpdates.impact: Required import for the StandardCharsets.UTF_8 constant used in the FileWriter fix.

failedUpdates.title: Upgrade log4j-core from 2.14.1 to 2.23+ for CVE-2021-44228 and Java 25 compatibility
failedUpdates.failureReason: Not needed: the build compiles successfully with log4j-core 2.14.1 on Java 25. The analysis lists this as an upgradeable dependency for CVE and potential Java 17+ reflection concerns, but it does not break the build. No runtime test was run (application not started per job constraints), so the potential reflection issue cannot be confirmed as a build failure.
failedUpdates.suggestedApproach: Upgrade log4j-core to 2.23.x or later to address CVE-2021-44228 (Log4Shell) and ensure full Java 25 compatibility. This should be done as a separate security-focused task.

failedUpdates.title: Upgrade commons-collections from 3.2.1 to 4.4 for CVE-2015-6420 and Java 25 compatibility
failedUpdates.failureReason: Not needed: the build compiles successfully with commons-collections 3.2.1 on Java 25. The analysis lists this as an upgradeable dependency for CVE and potential Java 25 compatibility concerns, but it does not break the build.
failedUpdates.suggestedApproach: Upgrade commons-collections to 4.4 to address CVE-2015-6420 (RCE via deserialization) and ensure Java 25 compatibility. This should be done as a separate security-focused task.

reportMetadata.description: Upgraded ResortsLite from Java 1.8/Spring Boot 2.7.18 to Java 25/Spring Boot 3.5.16. Fixed javax to jakarta migration, Java version, and charset encoding issues. Build compiles successfully.

postTransformationGuidelines: Spring Boot 3.5.16 brings Jakarta EE 9 (javax.* to jakarta.* namespace migration), Spring Security 6, Hibernate 6, and Tomcat 10. The javax.servlet.http.HttpSession import was migrated to jakarta.servlet.http.HttpSession as part of this required migration.
The application uses H2 in-memory database (already configured in application.properties and pom.xml) — no stand-in database was added. The database settings remain unchanged.

log4j-core (2.14.1) and commons-collections (3.2.1) were not upgraded as they do not break the build on Java 25. They are flagged as security concerns (CVE-2021-44228 and CVE-2015-6420) and should be upgraded in a separate security-focused task.
No tests exist in the project, so no test framework migration was needed.
